subject: Maintenance matrix alignment + fast-revert request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2025-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Maintenance matrix alignment + fast-revert request

Hi team,

We're scheduled to apply the next private-runtime micro-patch to Acme Cloud's VPC cluster on Wed 2025-10-22. Acme asked for a narrow 90-minute maintenance window and a clear fast-revert plan if we see KPIs degrade.

Ask: can infra and product confirm the attached maintenance_matrix_v2.xlsx is accurate for the runbook we intend to use? Specifics we need to lock down:
- Which node pools (by tag) will receive the pin bump first (canary slice)
- KV-cache warmup steps and expected time-to-warm per slice
- Circuit-breaker thresholds that trigger automated rollback
- Audit logging endpoints that must be reachable during the window for SOC evidence

Jonas: could you validate the network drain steps vs. Acme's subnet peering constraints?
Karthik: please confirm the rollback script in fast-revert-playbook.md will cleanly revert model pins and restore backed-up volumes within the SLA.
Neha: if we need an emergency hold, what's the fastest approval path to suspend the push?

Samantha (cc): sharing this early so we can align on blackout times and telemetry expectations. If Acme prefers, we can propose two possible 90-minute windows (UTC times in the sheet).

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: maintenance_matrix_v2.xlsx, fast-revert-playbook.md
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmecloud.com
Date: 2025-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Maintenance matrix alignment + fast-revert request

Thanks Naomi — we reviewed the matrix and the two proposed 90-minute windows look fine. A few clarifications from our side before we lock: 

1) Network: our peering has an inbound ACL that will drop ephemeral IPs unless they are pre-authorized. Can you confirm the rollout will only use the static management IPs listed (I added them inline in the sheet)?
2) Telemetry: during the canary slice we'd like a 15s token-level latency histogram and error-rate alerting to be forwarded to our PagerDuty group. Is that possible without additional instrumentation?
3) Rollback: we need the revert to include a DB schema compatibility check (our audit logs depend on a small schema tweak). If the revert script modifies service manifests, will it also revert that schema change or is that a separate DB migration rollback?

If you confirm the answers, I can get our legal/compliance to pre-approve the hold conditions (helps speed Neha's approval).

Sam
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Cloud

Attachment: acme_qa_checklist.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-11T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Maintenance matrix alignment + fast-revert request

Sam — good questions, answered inline: 

1) Network/static IPs: confirmed. The maintenance_matrix_v2.xlsx now lists the static management IPs under "control-plane-egress". Rollout tooling will only use those ENIs; no ephemeral addresses will be opened. I will also add a preflight step to validate ACL entries 30 minutes before the window.

2) Telemetry: we can forward token-latency histograms at 15s granularity to your PD group via the existing metrics forwarder. It will add ~120KB/min during the canary slice (should be fine). We'll include a short-lived read-only port binding to your telemetry endpoint. Note: forwarding credentials are temporary and will be revoked after the window.

3) DB/schema: the only schema change in this patch is a non-destructive index addition. The fast-revert-playbook.md will reverse the manifest and drop the index if revert is triggered, but we will not run a destructive down-migration automatically. Revert will restore the prior manifest and re-point the app to the pre-patch index. If you require a separate automated DB rollback, we need an explicit sign-off (and a backup snapshot schedule).

Operational notes and changes I've made to the sheet: added a separate "revert_kpi" column and explicit circuit-breaker thresholds (5% error-rate OR 2x median latency for 3 samples). Also added a preflight checklist item: DB snapshot at T-minus 45 minutes.

Naomi / Karthik / Neha: please confirm acceptance of those thresholds or propose changes. If accepted, Sam — can you sign off by EOD Monday so we can schedule the dry-run next week?

- Jonas
Director, Release Engineering
Redwood Inference

Quoted message below for context:
> On 2025-10-11 09:12, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> > We're scheduled to apply the next private-runtime micro-patch to Acme Cloud's VPC cluster on Wed 2025-10-22...
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-11T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Maintenance matrix alignment + fast-revert request

A few operational confirmations from my side: 

- Fast-revert: the script referenced in fast-revert-playbook.md will revert model pins, restore the previous container image tag, and trigger a workflow to reattach the last known-good volumes. Estimated RTO: 8-12 minutes for the service (depends on cold-start of KV cache).
- DB index: Jonas is correct — dropping an index is unsafe as an automated step. We'll plan the DB index removal to be manual with a safe guard (hold state) in the runbook. The revert will skip DB DDL rollback unless we get explicit DB rollback approval.
- Circuit-breaker: the rollback will be triggered automatically if the error-rate crosses 5% for three successive 1-minute buckets or if p50 latency doubles for 3 successive samples. We'll also add an operator override to force an immediate revert.
- Dry-run: recommend a dry-run in our staging replica on Tue 2025-10-21 (two days before) with a simulated traffic profile. That will validate the cold-cache hit and the revert path.

Naomi: I'll update fast-revert-playbook.md with the RTO estimate and the operator override steps by EOD. Sam — if those constraints work for you, please reply here and we will lock the window and schedule the dry-run.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Karthik's note: see updated playbook in the shared Drive link above.
